sites.home_text:
Shu Ding 
Making things at Vercel . My interests span a broad spectrum of subjects, encompassing visual, web, math, game design, and HCI. 
Since high school, I’ve spent years on algorithm competitions, web design and development. In 2017, I earned my BSc degree in Computer Science from Fudan University in Shanghai, and joined as a software engineer at Microsoft. In 2018, I joined Vercel (ZEIT) and worked on the core platform, Next.js, AI SDK, v0, and more. 
You can gain further insights into my background and interests through my thoughts , projects , find me on GitHub , X (Twitter) , and LinkedIn .

subpages.https://shud.in/projects:
Projects 
Over the years, I’ve had the privilege of working with talented teams on projects from open-source libraries to large-scale applications. 
 # 
I’ve been a core maintainer of Next.js since 2020, working closely with the React team. I led the development of Streaming SSR, Edge Runtime, React Server Components, Server Actions and other architectural improvements ( full contribution list ). I also designed and built the Next.js website in 2018 . 
 # 
I co-created v0 with Jared Palmer , Max Leiter , and shadcn in 2023, helped design its architecture, and implemented parts of the core AI, streaming, rendering pipeline and Design Mode. 
 # 
I designed the first client-side hook APIs and implemented function calling, RSC and data APIs for AI SDK . I also built the initial AI playground and documentation site . 
 # 
I joined Vercel in 2018 as one of the earliest engineers. Notable work includes:
 Fast Image Generation , Analytics Visualizations , Dashboard Performance Improvements , Project-Level Git Integration , Custom Production Branch , Usage Dashboard, Advanced Project Settings, Monorepo Pipeline, Deploy Button, Dashboard Redesign, etc. 
 # React Best Practices 
I created React Best Practices in 2026, a framework of 40+ performance rules for React and Next.js, for developers and AI agents ( announcement ). 
 # 
I created SWR with Guillermo Rauch in 2019 as the first hook-based, stale-while-revalidate data fetching library. Evil Rabbit and Paco Coursey designed the delightful SWR logo. 
 # Satori 
 Satori is the first CSS-to-SVG render engine that doesn’t need a browser. I created it in 2021 for Vercel’s OG Image Generation . 
Balancing size, performance and compatibility, Satori has become the standard way to generate social cards in Web frameworks such as Next.js , Nuxt.js , SvelteKit , Astro , and more. 
 # COBE 
 COBE is perhaps the smallest (5kB) 3D globe for the web, with a minimal style. I made it in 2021 to speed up Vercel’s homepage ( story ), and it has become a popular choice for many websites. 
 # GPU Lexer 
 GPU Lexer is a neural network-powered syntax highlighter that leverages WebGPU for fast lexing in the browser, and it's language-agnostic. 
 # 
 Nextra is one of the most popular Next.js-based documentation solutions; before it, Next.js had no good option. I created it in 2020 and led Nextra v2 in 2022, which powers many of my projects’ homepages. 
 # React Wrap Balancer 
 React Wrap Balancer was created in 2022 to improve typesetting on the Vercel blog, and was later ported to Vue and Svelte. I believe it helped push forward the CSS standard text - wrap : balance . 
 # Next View Transitions 
In 2024, I created Next View Transitions as the View Transitions API was becoming stable. 
Fun projects with original ideas: 
 Zero.js 
 Better All 
 Composable SVG Shaders 
 Frosted Glass 
 Legid: Safe & Legit ID Generator 
 BIDC: Bidirectional Channels 
 Scroll Indicator 
 Color Picker 
 Blur Slider 
Other mini projects (all on GitHub

Run `pnpm install` to install the project's dependencies. ### Build `nextra` ```bash pnpm --filter nextra build ``` Watch mode: `pnpm --filter nextra dev` ### Build `nextra-theme-docs` ```bash pnpm --filter nextra-theme-docs build ``` ### Development You can also debug them together with a website locally. For instance, to start `examples/docs` locally, run ```bash pnpm --filter example-docs dev ``` Any change to `example/docs` will be re-rendered instantly. If you update the core or theme packages, a rebuild is required. Or you can use the watch mode for both Nextra and the theme in separated terminals. ## Sponsors

## Introduction SWR is a React Hooks library for data fetching. The name “**SWR**” is derived from `stale-while-revalidate`, a cache invalidation strategy popularized by [HTTP RFC 5861](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5861). **SWR** first returns the data from cache (stale), then sends the request (revalidate), and finally comes with the up-to-date data again. With just one hook, you can significantly simplify the data fetching logic in your project. And it also covered in all aspects of speed, correctness, and stability to help you build better experiences: - **Fast**, **lightweight** and **reusable** data fetching - Transport and protocol agnostic - Built-in **cache** and request deduplication - **Real-time** experience - Revalidation on focus - Revalidation on network recovery - Polling - Pagination and scroll position recovery - SSR and SSG - Local mutation (Optimistic UI) - Built-in smart error retry - TypeScript - React Suspense - React Native ...and a lot more. With SWR, components will get **a stream of data updates constantly and automatically**. Thus, the UI will be always **fast** and **reactive**. --- **View full documentation and examples on [swr.vercel.app](https://swr.vercel.app).**
## Quick Start ```js import useSWR from 'swr' function Profile() { const { data, error, isLoading } = useSWR('/api/user', fetcher) if (error) return
failed to load
if (isLoading) return
loading...
return
hello {data.name}!
} ``` In this example, the React Hook `useSWR` accepts a `key` and a `fetcher` function. The `key` is a unique identifier of the request, normally the URL of the API.
